$comment: Layer 10 (Provider abstraction + mock adapter) canonical shape, discriminated by a top-level `llm_service` key -- another schema for conformance/agent/'s own directory (alongside the unified, transform, tool-registry, and agent-inbox shapes), not a fourth canonical family: scenarios here exercise the real LlmService/Adapter registration/resolution/dispatch seam directly, not a full agent-loop turn (L10-R004).

queries.$comment: Evaluated once, after every step has run, in the same 'steps mutate, queries observe' split tool-registry-scenario.schema.json already establishes -- neither kind of query itself mutates registration state. `introspect` is a pure read. `resolve` dispatches one real request through the public stream() seam (the only public way to observe which adapter a resolved identity actually reaches, since LlmService exposes no separate lookup-only method) and observes which adapter received it, rather than inspecting private registry state directly -- an UNRESOLVABLE identity is expected to raise before that dispatch, observed as `found: false`, not a step failure. A steps[].stream action is a SEPARATE, explicitly named observable action (it may settle a real stream with an in-band error, the specific behavior L10-R003/L10-R004 need to discriminate), so its own outcome is recorded under its own `as` id at the point it runs, not folded into this array.

behavior.$comment: `ok` produces an ordinary completed response (stop_reason stop). `reject` is an EXPECTED, adapter-detected failure at stream-creation time (e.g. invalid provider configuration) -- pinned Pi's own StreamFunction contract requires this to settle IN-BAND, as a returned stream whose terminal is an error chunk, never a raised/eagerly-typed exception (L10-R003).

reject_message.description: Required when behavior is reject; the in-band error_message the settled terminal must carry.

streamExpectation.$comment: The observable outcome of a `steps[].stream` action, keyed by its own `as` id. `settled: ok`/`error` means LlmService.stream() returned a stream whose (only) terminal has that stop_reason -- an in-band settlement, never an eager exception (L10-R003's own required discriminating dimension: an adapter's own EXPECTED, detected-at-invocation failure -- `behavior: reject` above -- must settle this way, not raise). `raised: true` means the call raised before any stream existed at all -- the ONLY legitimate case is an UNRESOLVABLE identity (AI-029's own eager full-identity-lookup check); a scenario must never expect `raised: true` for a resolved identity's own adapter-detected failure.
